structured_output.hypothesis: At equal area, oceanic-island regions hold markedly fewer native species than mainland regions, and this deficit persists after statistically controlling for climate and topography.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using native vascular-plant checklist richness S and area A, fit log10(S) = a + b*log10(A) + c*[oceanic island] (+ controls for latitude, mean annual temperature, annual precipitation, elevation range) across all GIFT regions with area between 10 and 100,000 km2. The claim passes if the oceanic-island coefficient c is negative with 95% CI excluding 0 in both the area-only model and the climate/topography-controlled model, and the controlled estimate is c <= -0.20 (at least ~37% fewer species than equal-area mainland regions). It must also hold in at least 3 of 4 area bins (10-100, 100-1,000, 1,000-10,000, 10,000-100,000 km2) in direction, with a bin-wise median richness ratio island/mainland < 0.8.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if the controlled c is > -0.10, or its 95% CI includes 0, or the sign is positive; or if the island deficit appears in fewer than 3 of 4 area bins, or the median island/mainland richness ratio is >= 0.8 in two or more bins.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'species of all kinds' is operationalised by native vascular-plant richness, the taxon best covered by a global regional-checklist database; this is a proxy, and other taxa (birds, insects, reptiles) are not tested. 'Oceanic islands' means islands never connected to a continent (volcanic or coral islands, not continental-shelf or continental fragments), taken from GIFT's island-type classification, and 'equal continental areas' means mainland regions of the same area. 'Not explained by physical conditions' is rendered as persistence of the deficit after controlling for climate, latitude and elevation range. The species-area-curve intercept replaces Darwin's informal comparison, and the modern habitat-diversity caveat is accounted for by the controls.

dataset.name: GIFT – Global Inventory of Floras and Traits
dataset.publisher: Biodiversity, Macroecology & Biogeography group, University of Göttingen
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT compiles regional plant checklists, covering both islands and mainland regions. It records the area of each region, whether it is an island and of what geological origin, and climate and elevation variables. Native species richness per region can be drawn with the GIFT R package (GIFT_checklists, GIFT_env, GIFT_shape). The fields used are native species richness, geo_entity area, island/geological-origin flag, latitude, mean annual temperature, annual precipitation and elevation range. This gives a direct species-area comparison between oceanic islands and mainland regions.
